backward_compat_traps.rule: RWDS is a variable-latency indicator during CA, a read strobe during reads, and a write byte mask during writes.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Treating RWDS as a single fixed-direction signal corrupts either latency selection, read capture, or write masking.

backward_compat_traps.rule: The CR0 initial-latency code (3..7) must be increased for higher clock frequencies.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Running at high frequency with a low latency code corrupts data capture.

backward_compat_traps.rule: Fixed = always 2x; variable = 1x/2x signalled by RWDS-during-CA.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Assuming fixed timing in a variable-latency configuration (ignoring RWDS during CA) mis-aligns the data phase.

backward_compat_traps.rule: The Command-Address is 48 bits sent MSB-byte-first over three clocks (six DDR bytes).
backward_compat_traps.trap: Truncating or mis-ordering the CA selects the wrong operation / address.

fields.spec_version: HyperBus Interface Specification (Cypress Semiconductor / Infineon Technologies)
previous_versions: Cypress HyperBus — original definition: differential CK/CK#, CS#, 8-bit DDR DQ[7:0], RWDS, 48-bit Command-Address, configurable latency, HyperRAM + HyperFlash.

key_changes.summary: HyperBus maintained by Infineon Technologies; the interface (CA format, RWDS roles, configurable latency, DDR DQ, HyperRAM/HyperFlash families, ID/Configuration registers) is carried forward unchanged.

fields.version_naming_history_note: HyperBus was defined by Cypress Semiconductor and is now maintained by Infineon Technologies (which acquired Cypress). The interface (differential clock, low pin count, 48-bit Command-Address, RWDS, configurable latency, HyperRAM and HyperFlash device families) is consistent across the Cypress and Infineon documentation.
